title: Between the Mines
intro: From now on you choose when to observe: press Observe (Enter) when the green meter peaks. Aim the packet with the arrow. Mines flank the target: if the measurement lands on one, you lose. Dispersion widens the packet faster than you expect, so a tighter launch is not always safer.
goal: Aim the arrow at the target, set speed and width, then press Observe when the green meter peaks. Mines sit on either side of the target.

physics.point: You choose when to look. A tighter launch is not more precise: a narrow packet spreads faster, so it arrives wider than a moderately wide one.

idea: Here you decide when the world looks. The meter P<sub>T</sub> is the chance that a look right now finds the particle in the target. It rises as the packet arrives, peaks, and falls as the packet passes and spreads.
Aiming is classical: the centre of the packet moves in a straight line at constant speed. Its size is not: a narrow packet carries a wide spread of speeds and smears out quickly.
Speed helps, because a packet that arrives sooner has had less time to spread. For a given flight time, the width rule from Rendezvous picks the best starting size.
maths: The target centre is 30.5 units from the launch point, at an angle of about −41°. At the top speed k = 2.4 the flight takes t ≈ 12.7.
The width on arrival is smallest for σ₀ = √(t/2) ≈ 2.5, and is then √t ≈ 3.6, larger than the target (radius 2.6).
The game's best is also about 23 %, at t ≈ 12.2. A tight start is worse: σ₀ = 0.8 arrives with a width of about 8 and peaks at only 6 %.
try: With k = 2.4 and the arrow on the target, set σ = 0.8 and play. The best P<sub>T</sub> is about 6 %. Then try σ = 2.5: about 23 %.
Lower k to 1.8 and widen σ to about 2.9 for the longer flight. The best P<sub>T</sub> drops to about 18 %.
Observe late, at t ≈ 16. P<sub>T</sub> has fallen to about 3 %, and most of the probability has already been absorbed at the edge of the world.
